group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-09-13: 'Aldaz CM[au]' 138, 'Aldaz CM[au] AND WWOX' 38, 'Nunez MI[au] AND WWOX' 5.
group_assessment.weighting: Same laboratory as the other paper of this lot and the same standing: it cloned WWOX (its ref 7, Bednarek 2000), so it is primary for the GENE and made the reagent it uses, and it is not a primary group for the DISEASE this repository models - nothing here is neurological or developmental. The weighting consequence is sharper in this paper than in the ovarian one, and in the opposite direction on the two halves. The immunoblot observation is strengthened: the blot carries molecular-weight markers, a loaded NEG. lane on each of two gels, and a declared two-gel composite. The immunohistochemistry interpretation is weakened: this paper's IHC section contains no specificity control of any kind, and it is the paper the ovarian series cites for its immunostaining method. Nine authors, seven of them shared with the ovarian paper; the breast pathology contribution (Sahin, MD Anderson; Klein-Szanto and Page, Fox Chase) is external to the WWOX laboratory and is the part of this work that is genuinely third-party.

field_density.note: The hormonal frame this paper's Discussion rests on has a literature of ELEVEN papers in twenty-one years ('WWOX AND sex steroid'), and sixteen for 'WWOX AND estrogen receptor' - against 111 for WWOX and breast cancer. A near-empty intersection in a rare-disease mechanism is a signal and not an absence: the sex-steroid reading of WWOX has never been densely worked, and this paper is one of the papers that keeps it alive by restating it. The reagent-specificity intersection is still 1.

multihop.queue_id_deferral: 🔴 RESOLVED LATER IN THE SAME SESSION, and the sequence is recorded rather than smoothed over. My first draft addressed this debt to FT-178. Between my read of the queue (highest id FT-177) and my append, a peer minted FT-178 for PMID 28283473 - 54 lines, unstaged in this shared checkout - and the validator caught the collision exactly as designed: 'FT-178 is a live queue entry about a different paper'. Two routes were unsafe and were refused: committing full_text_queue_current.md with my own entry would have carried the peer's uncommitted hunk under my commit message, which is the authorship incident scripts/legend_commit.sh exists to prevent and which its directory guard cannot see for a shared FILE; and minting an id in the working tree while committing this manifest against it would have persisted a manifest whose queue address exists in no commit, so every later validation would fail on an unresolvable identifier - a worse and quieter defect. So both papers were committed with the debt declared and NO FT id, which the cross-check reports as UNCHECKED - neither passed nor blocked - with the entry text carried verbatim in the dossier appendix. The peer then landed FT-178 at commit 066b476, the file went quiet, and FT-179 was minted as ONE address for all four load-bearing antecedents so no identifier is duplicated across the two manifests. The declaration above now names it.

entries.proposition: FIGURE ATTESTATION, Figure 4 at native 1442x443, inspected at 4x per half and 6x on the first gel's control lane. This is the strongest reagent panel in the lot and it carries three things the ovarian paper's blot does not: a molecular-weight axis (marks at 39 kD and 31 kD, with the WWOX band running above 39 kD), a NEG. lane on EACH of the two gels - blank for WWOX while carrying actin in that same lane, so the control is demonstrably loaded - and a composite that is DECLARED in its own caption rather than left to be discovered. entries.proposition: FIGURE ATTESTATION, Figure 3 at native 1289x521: WWOX and ER on the same tumour, side by side. The WWOX panel is cytoplasmic and membranous with blue nuclei; the ER panel is unambiguously NUCLEAR in essentially every epithelial cell. 🔴 This is the one place in the lot showing that the detection system - DAB, this microscope, this scoring platform - resolves a nuclear signal perfectly well when the antigen is nuclear. entries.note: The table prints p = 0.003 for the ER row, which is the negative-plus-weak comparison the Results text also gives as p=0.003; the completely-negative-only comparison's p = 0.0054 appears in the Results and the Summary but not in the table. Two comparisons, two values, no discrepancy - unlike the ovarian paper's PR cell, and worth recording because I checked for the same defect here and did not find it.
